messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — saw a spike in GPU OOMs on prod-rt1 at 2026-03-18T10:12Z. Logs point to large workspace allocations rather than the usual KV growth. attaching a short tail from the replica logs

maya:
```
[10:12:03] oom: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[10:12:03] alloc: requested 384MB for workspace
[10:12:03] kernel_selector: chosen=fused_attn_fast (score: 0.92)
[10:12:04] kvcache: evicted 0 entries
[10:12:04] request: tokens=1124, batch_id=342
```

sam: Thanks. Any idea which kernel-selector rollout touched prod? I rolled a small preference change last night to favor fused_attn for latency wins (commit 0f3a9c) — could be related.

kai: If the workspace allocation is the culprit, short-term mitigation: reduce per-request workspace cap and turn on buffer reuse. Also bias the selector toward memory-friendly kernels until we finish profiling. Proposed quick patch:

kai:
```json
{
  "workspace_size_mb": 512,
  "enable_buffer_reuse": true,
  "kernel_preference": "mem_saving",
  "max_batch_tokens": 4096
}
```

alex: +1 for conservative approach. Immediate routing fallback as safety: route requests with tokens > 800 to lm-small-quant (lower mem footprint) and enable a circuit breaker that trips when OOMs > 0.5% over 1m. That should buy headroom for investigation.

maya: Starting a canary rollout with workspace_size_mb=512 to 10% of prod-rt1 now. Will watch OOMs and p95.

ops-bot: [ALERT] Deploy started by maya at 2026-03-18T10:22Z — canary target=prod-rt1 (10%)

sam: While canary runs, let's also tweak batching heuristics: cap batch assembly to max_batch_tokens=4096 and prefer smaller batches when queue latency > 15ms to avoid oversized workspace spikes. I can push that as a short-lived heuristic flag.

kai: Add a tiny KV cache TTL jitter to avoid synchronized evictions under pressure. e.g. ttl_ms = base_ttl * (1 + rand(-0.1, 0.1)). Also enable aggressive KV soft-eviction for large requests.

alex: Good. Also make sure our prometheus alerts include 'workspace_allocated_bytes' per-replica and a circuit-breaker metric exported so SRE can auto-scale or temporarily divert traffic.

maya: Canary metrics after 12m: OOMs dropped to 0 on canary nodes, non-canary still saw 2 incidents. p95 latency on canary increased ~4% which is acceptable. Promoting canary to 50% now. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [INFO] Canary promotion by maya to 50% at 2026-03-18T10:34Z

sam: Filing a follow-up postmortem and attaching the profiling traces (heap/allocations + kernel selection logs). Need to identify why fused_attn increased transient workspace at certain seq lengths. Could be interaction with batching windows.

maya: Postmortem created: https://tickets.internal/RED-1234 — includes flamegraphs, heap snapshots, kernel selector diffs, and canary metric dashboards.

kai: Follow-ups: schedule a controlled stress test across token-length distributions, validate buffer reuse correctness under concurrent assignments, and run A/B comparing fused_attn vs mem_saving selector over 24h. Also add unit/regression tests that assert workspace <= threshold for edge token sizes.

alex: Also add a temporary runtime policy: any single allocation request > 256MB for workspace should be throttled or split (request shaping) unless explicitly flagged. We can relax after kernel selector review.

maya: Agreed. I'll add throttle rule to runtime config and coordinate with infra to run the stress tests tomorrow morning. Thanks all. :rocket:

sam: Thanks — remind me to block auto-promote on future kernel-selector changes until we have a smoke profile run covering mixed token lengths.

alex: Filed follow-up tasks in the ticket. Closing loop for now. :eyes:
